subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. OtherVendor - ACME procurement
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up & next steps

Marissa / team,

Thanks for the demo today — really useful. A quick recap from our side and what procurement will need to move to the bake-off stage: 

- Primary pain: incorrect or inconsistent outputs from current LLM provider leading to aborted flows and manual intervention.
- Goals: reduce error rate on templated responses by 90% within production traffic; keep 95th percentile latency under 350ms for 1–2k rps.
- Decision criteria (high-level): accuracy/QA on our test prompts, latency under load, security/compliance posture (SOC2 + data residency), TCO over 12 months.

Procurement wants a structured bake-off matrix comparing Redwood vs. OtherVendor (functional pass/fail per test, latency percentiles, cost estimate). Can you share a template and proposed validation tests? Also please attach the recording.

Next steps from ACME: procurement will issue an NDA (if needed) and a short SOW for the bake-off week; target to complete tech validation by Nov 30.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Integrations, ACME Corp

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up & next steps

Alex — really great to speak today, appreciate the clarity on goals. Quick recap + attached bake-off template and suggested test-suite.

Key pain points we heard:
- Inconsistent templated outputs (high human fallback)
- Latency spikes at 95th percentile under burst traffic
- Lack of automated observability tied to prompt-level quality regressions

What we propose for the bake-off (summary):
1) Controlled pass/fail suite: 200 representative prompts across your top 6 flows (we suggest the sheet attached).
2) Load window: 1k steady RPS + two 5-minute bursts to 2.5k to measure KV cache behavior.
3) Quality metrics: exact-match + tolerance scoring and human-blind eval on 30 random samples per flow.
4) Security/compliance checks: redact PII flow, retention/config validation, and a brief SOC2 evidence checklist.

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Filled bake-off matrix (we'll pre-populate with our expected results)
- Recording of the demo and a 1-page exec summary
- Access to a short-lived sandbox for the test week (managed instance in us-west-2)

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-sheet.xlsx (bake-off matrix & test cases), acme-demo-recording.mp4 (demo recording).

Proposed timeline:
- Nov 12: confirm NDA & SOW items
- Nov 15–19: run bake-off tests (tech team + Redwood engineer on-call)
- Nov 22: joint review of results

Open questions for ACME (can you confirm):
- Will procurement require a vendor security questionnaire (we can pre-fill standard sections)?
- Do you have any additional PII redaction rules specific to the templated flows?
- Who will be the primary technical contact for test orchestration?

I'll loop in Rishi and Steph to coordinate the sandbox and testing schedule. Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
